title: platform-checklist: retire the drag-reorder step and acceptance clause of platform-core.shell-nav-personalization — end users do not reorder the runtime sidebar (maintainer ruling 2026-10-09)
body:
## Ruling

**The maintainer, in chat on 2026-10-09** (session `64cb68a6-01c7-4dc6-acc6-ccb459c90ef2`), verbatim:

> 右侧浏览器，左侧菜单在用户界面不应该显示拖动按钮，拖动设计是studio的工作。

End users do not reorder the runtime sidebar; navigation order is authored in Studio. The implementation change is objectstack-ai/objectui#12059.

## What to change

`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json`, item `platform-core.shell-nav-personalization` (revision 1):
- **Remove** step 3, `drag-reorder: reorder nav items by drag (UnifiedSidebar useNavOrder, enableReorder / onReorder=handleReorder); reload — the order persists (localStorage per-app key)`, and the acceptance clause that verifies it (acceptance[2], the one objectstack-ai/objectui#11626 was filed against).
- **Optionally replace it** with a negative clause: the runtime sidebar draws no drag grip (`aria-roledescription="sortable"`), and the rendered order is the app's authored order.
- **Drop "reorder"** from the item's title and from the "record which persistence each feature uses" step ("reorder + collapse are local" becomes "collapse is local"). Bump `revision`.
- **Unchanged:** collapse, pin/unpin, favorites, recents and breadcrumbs.

Why now: if the checklist keeps the clause, the next release run fails it again and re-files objectui#11626's opposite.
